# CLI reference

Every command and option of the Exasol Launcher, taken from the launcher itself. Run
`exasol <command> --help` to see the same text locally.

Paths shown as `<home>` refer to your home directory.

## Options available on every command

These options are accepted by `exasol` and by every subcommand, so they are listed here
instead of being repeated below.

```text
      --auto-approve       Approve confirmation prompts, which a run with no terminal also does automatically except for local runtime host preparation. Input validation and other safety checks still apply
      --log-level string   Set log level: debug, info, warn, error
```

`-h`, `--help` prints the help for the command it follows.

## `exasol` { data-toc-label="exasol" }

```text
Exasol Personal: https://github.com/exasol/exasol-personal

Getting Started:
	To create and run an Exasol deployment, run "exasol install <infra preset name-or-path>".
	This single command initializes your deployment directory, prepares the selected infrastructure,
	and installs the database. It uses either a built-in infrastructure preset or a custom preset
	at a path you provide. Built-in presets are: local, aws, azure, exoscale, and stackit.

	Quick start: exasol install local
	Deployment lifecycle: install -> status -> connect -> stop -> start

	If you do not pass --deployment-dir and are not already inside a deployment directory,
	the Exasol Launcher uses <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/default. Pass --deployment-dir
	to override the active deployment directory, or pass --deployment <name> (-d <name>) to use
	<home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> instead, for running more than one deployment
	side by side. --deployment-dir and --deployment cannot be used together.

	Note: Cloud presets require provider credentials in your environment.
	Use "exasol init --help", "exasol install --help", or "exasol presets list" to see the preset
	compatibility matrix.

	AI agent skills: https://github.com/exasol-labs/exasol-agent-skills

Usage:
	exasol [command] [flags]

Essential Commands:
	config      Manage deployment configuration
	deploy      Deploy using an existing deployment directory
	init        Initialize a new deployment directory
	install     Initialize, apply configuration, and deploy Exasol in one step

Lifecycle Commands:
	destroy     Destroy a deployment
	remove      Remove a local deployment directory without destroying resources
	start       Start a deployment
	stop        Stop a deployment

Additional Commands:
	cache       Manage the runtime artifact cache
	completion  Generate the autocompletion script for the specified shell
	connect     Open an SQL connection to a running database
	deployments Manage launcher-managed deployment directories
	diag        Diagnostic tools for an active deployment
	info        Prints information about your Exasol deployment.
	presets     Manage embedded presets
	shell       Shell access to deployment host and container
	slc         Manage script language containers (SLCs)
	status      Get the status of a deployment
	version     Print the program version and exit

Examples:
  exasol install local
```

## Essential Commands

### `exasol config` { data-toc-label="config" }

```text
Manage deployment configuration

	Inspect, patch, or reset configuration parameters for the presets already
	initialized in the deployment directory. Configuration changes preserve local
	infrastructure state. Run exasol deploy after changing configuration to apply
	the changes to the deployment.

Usage:
	exasol config [command] [flags]

Additional Commands:
	get                           Show active deployment configuration
	reset                         Reset deployment configuration options to defaults
	set                           Update deployment configuration options
```

#### `exasol config get` { data-toc-label="config get" }

```text
Show active deployment configuration

Usage:
	exasol config get [option-name...] [flags]

Flags:
  -d, --deployment string          Select <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> as the deployment directory
      --deployment-dir file-path   Override the deployment directory selected automatically
  -j, --json                       Output in JSON format
```

#### `exasol config reset` { data-toc-label="config reset" }

```text
Reset deployment configuration options to defaults

Usage:
	exasol config reset [option-name...] [flags]

Flags:
      --all                        Reset all options to defaults
  -d, --deployment string          Select <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> as the deployment directory
      --deployment-dir file-path   Override the deployment directory selected automatically
```

#### `exasol config set` { data-toc-label="config set" }

```text
Update deployment configuration options

Usage:
	exasol config set [flags]

Flags:
  -d, --deployment string          Select <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> as the deployment directory
      --deployment-dir file-path   Override the deployment directory selected automatically
```

### `exasol deploy` { data-toc-label="deploy" }

```text
Deploy using an existing deployment directory

Once a deployment is complete, Terraform state files will be stored in the deployment directory.
Do not delete the deployment directory until the `destroy` command has been executed.

Usage:
	exasol deploy [flags]

Flags:
  -d, --deployment string          Select <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> as the deployment directory
      --deployment-dir file-path   Override the deployment directory selected automatically
  -v, --verbose                    Enable verbose output for deployment actions
```

### `exasol init` { data-toc-label="init" }

```text
Initialize a new deployment directory

	Extracts the specified infrastructure and installation presets into the deployment directory.
	For an already initialized deployment with the same presets, supplied configuration
	flags update only the selected parameters. Omitted parameters keep their values.
	To switch presets, run exasol destroy --remove first, or exasol remove if the
	deployment resources are already gone.
	If --deployment-dir is not provided and the current directory is not a deployment directory,
	uses <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/default. Pass --deployment <name> (-d <name>) to use
	<home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> instead.

	Preset arguments:
	  - The first argument selects the infrastructure preset (required).
	  - The optional second argument selects the installation preset.

	Each argument can be either an embedded preset name (e.g. "aws") or a preset directory path.
	To force path selection, pass a path-like value such as "./my-preset" or "/abs/path/to/preset".

	Tip: use "exasol presets" to discover and export presets.
	
	Available infrastructure presets: aws, azure, exoscale, local, stackit
	Available installation presets: local, ubuntu

	Compatibility matrix (embedded presets):
	  infrastructure  local  ubuntu
	  aws             no     yes   
	  azure           no     yes   
	  exoscale        no     yes   
	  local           yes    no    
	  stackit         no     yes

Usage:
	exasol init <infra preset name-or-path> [install preset name-or-path] [flags]

Flags:
  -d, --deployment string           Select <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> as the deployment directory
      --deployment-dir file-path    Override the deployment directory selected automatically
      --no-launcher-version-check   Disable automatic version checking for new launcher releases

Examples:
  exasol init aws
  exasol init aws ubuntu
  exasol init ./my-infra-preset ./my-install-preset
```

`exasol init` also accepts the variables of the selected preset. Each preset below adds these flags to the ones listed above.

#### `exasol init aws` { data-toc-label="aws" }

```text
Infrastructure variable flags of preset `aws`:
      --adminui-password string   Optional Admin UI password. If empty, a random password is generated (default: "")
      --cluster-size number       Number of nodes in the cluster (use 1 for single-node deployment) (default: 1)
      --data-volume-size number   Size in GB for the database data volume (default: 100)
      --db-password string        Optional database password. If empty, a random password is generated (default: "")

      --os-volume-size number     Size in GB for the OS/root volume (default: 100)
      --s3-archive-enabled        Enable remote archive/backup integration: creates S3 bucket, IAM user/access keys, SSM params, and VPC S3 endpoint. (default: true)
      --volume-type string        EBS volume type for both OS and data volumes (default: "gp3")

Installation variable flags of preset `ubuntu`:
```

```text
      --no-db-version-check     Disable the daily database version check (C4). (default: false)
```

### `exasol install` { data-toc-label="install" }

```text
Initialize, apply configuration, and deploy Exasol in one step

	Initializes the deployment directory or applies supplied configuration, prepares infrastructure,
	and installs Exasol.
	Rerunning install with the same presets is safe for retrying failed deployments.
	To switch presets, run exasol destroy --remove first, or exasol remove if the
	deployment resources are already gone.
	If --deployment-dir is not provided and the current directory is not a deployment directory,
	uses <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/default. Pass --deployment <name> (-d <name>) to use
	<home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> instead.

	Preset arguments:
	  - The first argument selects the infrastructure preset (required).
	  - The optional second argument selects the installation preset.

	Each argument can be either an embedded preset name (e.g. "aws") or a preset directory path.
	To force path selection, pass a path-like value such as "./my-preset" or "/abs/path/to/preset".

	Tip: use "exasol presets" to discover and export presets.
	
	Available infrastructure presets: aws, azure, exoscale, local, stackit
	Available installation presets: local, ubuntu

	Compatibility matrix (embedded presets):
	  infrastructure  local  ubuntu
	  aws             no     yes   
	  azure           no     yes   
	  exoscale        no     yes   
	  local           yes    no    
	  stackit         no     yes

Usage:
	exasol install <infra preset name-or-path> [install preset name-or-path] [flags]

Flags:
  -d, --deployment string           Select <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> as the deployment directory
      --deployment-dir file-path    Override the deployment directory selected automatically
      --no-launcher-version-check   Disable automatic version checking for new launcher releases
  -v, --verbose                     Enable verbose output for deployment actions

Examples:
  exasol install aws
  exasol install aws ubuntu
```

`exasol install` also accepts the variables of the selected preset. Each preset below adds these flags to the ones listed above.

## Lifecycle Commands

### `exasol destroy` { data-toc-label="destroy" }

```text
Destroy a deployment

Destroying a deployment deletes all resources - including all data.
If you want to retain any data, make sure you've created and moved backups to another safe location.
By default, local deployment files are kept so the same deployment can be inspected or recreated.
Pass --remove to remove the local deployment directory after deployment resources have been destroyed.

Usage:
	exasol destroy [flags]

Flags:
  -d, --deployment string          Select <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> as the deployment directory
      --deployment-dir file-path   Override the deployment directory selected automatically
      --remove                     Remove the local deployment directory after deployment resources are successfully destroyed
  -v, --verbose                    Enable verbose output for deployment actions
```

### `exasol remove` { data-toc-label="remove" }

```text
Remove a local deployment directory without destroying resources

This is a recovery command for cases where deployment resources were already deleted manually,
or where you no longer have access to destroy them through the launcher.

WARNING: This command removes the local deployment directory. It does not destroy
deployment resources and can make launcher-based cleanup impossible if resources still exist.

Usage:
	exasol remove [flags]

Flags:
  -d, --deployment string          Select <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> as the deployment directory
      --deployment-dir file-path   Override the deployment directory selected automatically
```

### `exasol start` { data-toc-label="start" }

```text
Start a deployment

Start a deployment after it has been stopped.
After the deployment starts, it will have a new public IP address and DNS name assigned.

This command now waits until the Exasol database becomes ready and can accept connections.
If the database does not become ready within the timeout, the command fails.

Usage:
	exasol start [flags]

Flags:
  -d, --deployment string          Select <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> as the deployment directory
      --deployment-dir file-path   Override the deployment directory selected automatically
  -j, --json                       Output in JSON format
  -v, --verbose                    Enable verbose output for deployment actions
      --wait-timeout-minutes int   Maximum minutes to wait for the database to become ready (default 30)
```

### `exasol stop` { data-toc-label="stop" }

```text
Stop a deployment

Stop a deployment without removing its configuration, data, or infrastructure.

Usage:
	exasol stop [flags]

Flags:
  -d, --deployment string          Select <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> as the deployment directory
      --deployment-dir file-path   Override the deployment directory selected automatically
  -j, --json                       Output in JSON format
  -v, --verbose                    Enable verbose output for deployment actions
```

## Additional Commands

### `exasol cache` { data-toc-label="cache" }

```text
Manage the runtime artifact cache

Runtime artifacts are launcher-managed tools and files that are downloaded on demand
and reused across deployments.

Usage:
	exasol cache [command] [flags]

Additional Commands:
	clean                         Clean cached runtime artifacts
	list                          List cached runtime artifacts
	unlock                        Clear a stale runtime artifact cache lock
```

#### `exasol cache clean` { data-toc-label="cache clean" }

```text
Clean cached runtime artifacts.

With no selector, this removes artifacts older than the configured retention period.
Use --invalid to remove artifacts that fail integrity checks.
Use --all to remove every cached runtime artifact.
Use --partial-downloads to remove staged partial downloads.
Use --dry-run to preview a cleanup without removing files.

Usage:
	exasol cache clean [flags]

Flags:
      --all                 Remove all cached runtime artifacts
      --dry-run             Preview cleanup without removing files
      --invalid             Remove cached artifacts that fail integrity checks
      --partial-downloads   Remove staged partial downloads
```

#### `exasol cache list` { data-toc-label="cache list" }

```text
List cached runtime artifacts

Usage:
	exasol cache list [flags]

Flags:
  -j, --json   Output in JSON format
```

#### `exasol cache unlock` { data-toc-label="cache unlock" }

```text
Clear a stale runtime artifact cache lock.

Only use this command when you are certain that no launcher process is currently
using the runtime artifact cache.

Usage:
	exasol cache unlock [flags]
```

### `exasol completion` { data-toc-label="completion" }

```text
Generate the autocompletion script for exasol for the specified shell.
See each sub-command's help for details on how to use the generated script.

Usage:
	exasol completion [command] [flags]

Additional Commands:
	bash                          Generate the autocompletion script for bash
	fish                          Generate the autocompletion script for fish
	powershell                    Generate the autocompletion script for powershell
	zsh                           Generate the autocompletion script for zsh
```

??? note "`exasol completion bash`"

    ```text
    Generate the autocompletion script for the bash shell.

    This script depends on the 'bash-completion' package.
    If it is not installed already, you can install it via your OS's package manager.

    To load completions in your current shell session:

    	source <(exasol completion bash)

    To load completions for every new session, execute once:

    #### Linux:

    	exasol completion bash > /etc/bash_completion.d/exasol

    #### macOS:

    	exasol completion bash > $(brew --prefix)/etc/bash_completion.d/exasol

    You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

    Usage:
    	exasol completion bash

    Flags:
          --no-descriptions   disable completion descriptions
    ```

??? note "`exasol completion fish`"

    ```text
    Generate the autocompletion script for the fish shell.

    To load completions in your current shell session:

    	exasol completion fish | source

    To load completions for every new session, execute once:

    	exasol completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/exasol.fish

    You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

    Usage:
    	exasol completion fish [flags]

    Flags:
          --no-descriptions   disable completion descriptions
    ```

??? note "`exasol completion powershell`"

    ```text
    Generate the autocompletion script for powershell.

    To load completions in your current shell session:

    	exasol completion powershell | Out-String | Invoke-Expression

    To load completions for every new session, add the output of the above command
    to your powershell profile.

    Usage:
    	exasol completion powershell [flags]

    Flags:
          --no-descriptions   disable completion descriptions
    ```

??? note "`exasol completion zsh`"

    ```text
    Generate the autocompletion script for the zsh shell.

    If shell completion is not already enabled in your environment you will need

    to enable it.  You can execute the following once:

    	echo "autoload -U compinit; compinit" >> ~/.zshrc

    To load completions in your current shell session:

    	source <(exasol completion zsh)

    To load completions for every new session, execute once:

    #### Linux:

    	exasol completion zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_exasol"

    #### macOS:

    	exasol completion zsh > $(brew --prefix)/share/zsh/site-functions/_exasol

    You will need to start a new shell for this setup to take effect.

    Usage:
    	exasol completion zsh [flags]

    Flags:
          --no-descriptions   disable completion descriptions
    ```

### `exasol connect` { data-toc-label="connect" }

```text
Open an SQL connection to a running database

Establish an SQL connection to the database instance in an active deployment.
When run non-interactively with --json, stdout contains one JSON document for
the full invocation. Statement records include statementType and rowsAffected;
result-set statements report rowsAffected as 0 when the driver does not expose
affected-row metadata. Interactive --json sessions continue to print one JSON
document per executed statement instead of an invocation envelope.

Usage:
	exasol connect [flags]

Flags:
  -c, --command string             Execute the given semicolon-separated SQL statement(s) and exit
      --csv                        Output in CSV format
  -d, --deployment string          Select <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> as the deployment directory
      --deployment-dir file-path   Override the deployment directory selected automatically
      --execute-on-semicolon       Execute SQL only after semicolon terminators are entered (default true)
  -f, --file string                Execute the semicolon-separated SQL statements from the given file and exit
  -k, --insecure                   Skip server certificate verification
  -j, --json string[="pretty"]     Output in JSON format: pretty, compact (default "pretty")
      --max-rows int               Maximum rows to display per query (0 = unlimited; default: 100 interactively, unlimited otherwise) (default -1)
  -p, --password string            Database password
  -u, --username string            Database username (default "sys")

Examples:
  exasol connect
  exasol connect --json
  exasol connect --csv -c "SELECT * FROM products" > products.csv
  exasol connect -c "SELECT 1; SELECT 2"
  exasol connect -f script.sql
  printf 'SELECT 1;\n' | exasol connect --json=compact
```

### `exasol deployments` { data-toc-label="deployments" }

```text
Manage launcher-managed deployment directories

Deployment directories are the launcher-managed directories under
<home>/.exasol/personal/deployments: the default deployment directory and any
named deployment directory selected via --deployment/-d. This does not include
deployment directories selected via an arbitrary --deployment-dir path.

Usage:
	exasol deployments [command] [flags]

Additional Commands:
	list                          List launcher-managed deployment directories
```

#### `exasol deployments list` { data-toc-label="deployments list" }

```text
List launcher-managed deployment directories

Usage:
	exasol deployments list [flags]

Flags:
  -j, --json   Output in JSON format
```

### `exasol diag` { data-toc-label="diag" }

```text
Diagnostic tools for an active deployment

Includes subcommands for deployment configuration inspection and recovery tooling.

Usage:
	exasol diag [command] [flags]

Additional Commands:
	cache                         Inspect the runtime artifact cache
	info                          Print all deployment info
	local                         Report local deployment runtime and reachability state
	unlock                        Unlock a deployment.
```

#### `exasol diag cache` { data-toc-label="diag cache" }

```text
Inspect the runtime artifact cache.

This command reports cache state without removing artifacts, rewriting metadata,
or clearing cache locks.

Usage:
	exasol diag cache [flags]
```

#### `exasol diag info` { data-toc-label="diag info" }

```text
Print all deployment info

The output is formatted as JSON.

Usage:
	exasol diag info [flags]

Flags:
  -d, --deployment string          Select <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> as the deployment directory
      --deployment-dir file-path   Override the deployment directory selected automatically
```

#### `exasol diag local` { data-toc-label="diag local" }

```text
Report local deployment runtime and reachability state

Reports local VM status, reported guest IP, bound host ports, per-port
forwarder reachability, database readiness, and local platform support.
Safe to run at any time, whether or not the deployment is currently running.

The output is formatted as JSON.

Usage:
	exasol diag local [flags]

Flags:
  -d, --deployment string          Select <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> as the deployment directory
      --deployment-dir file-path   Override the deployment directory selected automatically
```

#### `exasol diag unlock` { data-toc-label="diag unlock" }

```text
Get the status of a deployment

	The lock file will be removed.

	The lock file prevents multiple instances of the exasol launcher running simultaneously.
	Unlocking the directory may cause inconsistent file states in the deployment directory.

Usage:
	exasol diag unlock [flags]

Flags:
  -d, --deployment string          Select <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> as the deployment directory
      --deployment-dir file-path   Override the deployment directory selected automatically
```

### `exasol info` { data-toc-label="info" }

```text
Prints information about your Exasol deployment.

You can use the '--json' option to print the output in JSON format.

Example usage:
    exasol info
    exasol info --json

Usage:
	exasol info [flags]

Flags:
  -d, --deployment string          Select <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> as the deployment directory
      --deployment-dir file-path   Override the deployment directory selected automatically
  -j, --json                       Output in JSON format
```

### `exasol presets` { data-toc-label="presets" }

```text
Manage embedded presets

Presets are pre-defined configurations used by commands like "init" and "install".

Use "exasol presets list" to see what presets are available.

Usage:
	exasol presets [command] [flags]

Additional Commands:
	export                        Export an embedded preset to a directory
	list                          List available presets
```

#### `exasol presets export` { data-toc-label="presets export" }

```text
Export an embedded preset to a local directory.

The target directory must exist and be empty.

By default, the current working directory is used.

Usage:
	exasol presets export <preset> [flags]

Flags:
      --to string     Target directory to export to (must be empty)
  -t, --type string   Preset type (use when the same preset name exists for multiple types)
```

#### `exasol presets list` { data-toc-label="presets list" }

```text
List available embedded presets.

By default, the output is human-readable.
Use the '--json' option to print the output in JSON format.

Usage:
	exasol presets list [flags]

Flags:
  -j, --json          Output in JSON format
  -t, --type string   Filter by preset type: infrastructure, installation
```

### `exasol shell` { data-toc-label="shell" }

```text
Shell access to deployment host and container

Includes subcommands for host OS shell and COS container shell access.

Usage:
	exasol shell [command] [flags]

Additional Commands:
	container                     Establish an interactive COS container shell connection
	host                          Establish a secure shell connection to a host node
```

#### `exasol shell container` { data-toc-label="shell container" }

```text
Establish an interactive COS container shell connection

Creates an interactive COS container shell connection in the active deployment.
COS is cluster-scoped and uses the access node.

Usage:
	exasol shell container [flags]

Flags:
  -d, --deployment string          Select <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> as the deployment directory
      --deployment-dir file-path   Override the deployment directory selected automatically
```

#### `exasol shell host` { data-toc-label="shell host" }

```text
Establish a secure shell connection to a host node

Creates a secure host OS shell connection to a node in the active deployment.
If no specific node is specified, connects to the first node available.

Usage:
	exasol shell host [flags]

Flags:
  -d, --deployment string          Select <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> as the deployment directory
      --deployment-dir file-path   Override the deployment directory selected automatically
  -n, --node string                Name of the node to connect to. Connects to the first available node if not specified
```

### `exasol slc` { data-toc-label="slc" }

```text
Manage script language containers (SLCs)

Script language containers provide the language runtimes used by UDFs.
Local deployments ship without any SLC installed; install one to run UDFs in that language.

Usage:
	exasol slc [command] [flags]

Additional Commands:
	custom                        Manage user-supplied (custom) script language containers
	install                       Install an official script language container
	list                          List available script language containers and which are installed
	remove                        Remove a script language container
	update                        Update an installed official script language container
```

#### `exasol slc custom` { data-toc-label="slc custom" }

```text
Manage user-supplied (custom) script language containers

Usage:
	exasol slc custom [command] [flags]

Additional Commands:
	install     Install a custom script language container
	update      Replace an installed custom script language container
```

##### `exasol slc custom install` { data-toc-label="slc custom install" }

```text
Install a custom script language container

Usage:
	exasol slc custom install [flags]

Flags:
      --alias string               Alias for the custom SLC (used in CREATE <alias> SCALAR SCRIPT)
  -d, --deployment string          Select <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> as the deployment directory
      --deployment-dir file-path   Override the deployment directory selected automatically
  -j, --json                       Output in JSON format
      --language string            Language identifier provided by the custom SLC client (normalized to lowercase)
      --no-restart                 Record the custom SLC without restarting; it activates on the next start
      --source string              Container tarball to install: a local path or an HTTPS URL
  -v, --verbose                    Enable verbose output for deployment actions
```

##### `exasol slc custom update` { data-toc-label="slc custom update" }

```text
Replace an installed custom script language container

Usage:
	exasol slc custom update [flags]

Flags:
      --alias string               Alias of the custom SLC to update
  -d, --deployment string          Select <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> as the deployment directory
      --deployment-dir file-path   Override the deployment directory selected automatically
  -j, --json                       Output in JSON format
      --language string            Override the custom SLC language identifier (normalized to lowercase)
      --no-restart                 Record the update without restarting; it applies on the next start
      --source string              Container tarball to update to: a local path or an HTTPS URL
  -v, --verbose                    Enable verbose output for deployment actions
```

#### `exasol slc install` { data-toc-label="slc install" }

```text
Install an official script language container by alias or flavor.
Prefer aliases because they remain stable when the catalog flavor changes.

The alias `rust` is special: it is not part of the official catalogue. It installs
the latest release of exasol-labs/language-container-rs that matches this machine's
CPU architecture. To install a specific Rust build instead, use
`exasol slc custom install --language rust --source <path-or-url>`.

For any other user-supplied container, use `exasol slc custom install`.

Usage:
	exasol slc install <alias-or-flavor> [flags]

Flags:
  -d, --deployment string          Select <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> as the deployment directory
      --deployment-dir file-path   Override the deployment directory selected automatically
  -j, --json                       Output in JSON format
      --no-restart                 Record the SLC without restarting; it activates on the next start
  -v, --verbose                    Enable verbose output for deployment actions
```

#### `exasol slc list` { data-toc-label="slc list" }

```text
List available script language containers and which are installed

Usage:
	exasol slc list [flags]

Flags:
  -d, --deployment string          Select <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> as the deployment directory
      --deployment-dir file-path   Override the deployment directory selected automatically
  -j, --json                       Output in JSON format
```

#### `exasol slc remove` { data-toc-label="slc remove" }

```text
Remove an installed script language container by alias.

Handles both official and user-supplied (custom) containers.

Usage:
	exasol slc remove <alias> [flags]

Flags:
  -d, --deployment string          Select <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> as the deployment directory
      --deployment-dir file-path   Override the deployment directory selected automatically
  -j, --json                       Output in JSON format
      --no-restart                 Record the removal without restarting; it applies on the next start
  -v, --verbose                    Enable verbose output for deployment actions
```

#### `exasol slc update` { data-toc-label="slc update" }

```text
Update an installed official script language container by alias or flavor.
Prefer aliases because they remain stable when the catalog flavor changes.

The alias `rust` is special: it re-resolves the latest release of
exasol-labs/language-container-rs for this machine's CPU architecture and applies it
if it differs from the installed container. To pin a specific Rust build, use
`exasol slc custom install --language rust --source <path-or-url>`.

For any other user-supplied container, use `exasol slc custom update`.

Usage:
	exasol slc update <alias-or-flavor> [flags]

Flags:
  -d, --deployment string          Select <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> as the deployment directory
      --deployment-dir file-path   Override the deployment directory selected automatically
  -j, --json                       Output in JSON format
      --no-restart                 Record the update without restarting; it applies on the next start
  -v, --verbose                    Enable verbose output for deployment actions
```

### `exasol status` { data-toc-label="status" }

```text
Get the status of a deployment

Display the status of the current deployment.

	The possible values for the `status` field are:

	- not_initialized
	- initialized
	- operation_in_progress
	- interrupted
	- stopped
	- running
	- deployment_failed
	- database_connection_failed
	- database_ready

Usage:
	exasol status [flags]

Flags:
  -d, --deployment string          Select <home>/.exasol/personal/deployments/<name> as the deployment directory
      --deployment-dir file-path   Override the deployment directory selected automatically
  -j, --json                       Output in JSON format
      --timeout int                Maximum number of seconds to wait for the complete status check (default 5)
      --unsafe                     Try to read the deployment folder state even if it is locked. May fail.
```

### `exasol version` { data-toc-label="version" }

```text
Print the program version and exit

Example usage:
    exasol version
    exasol version --latest --json

Usage:
	exasol version [flags]

Flags:
  -j, --json     Output in JSON format
  -l, --latest   Get information about the latest available version
```
